title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 180 (Suit by bailor or bailee against wrong-doer)

content.overview: Section 180 provides that if a third person wrongfully deprives the bailee of the use or possession of the goods bailed, or does them any injury, the bailee is entitled to use such remedies as the owner might have used in the like case if no bailment had been made; and either the bailor or the bailee may bring a suit against a third person for such deprivation or injury.
content.glance: Either the bailor or the bailee may sue a third person who wrongfully deprives the bailee of use or possession or injures the goods; the bailee may use the remedies the owner could have used.
content.study: If a third person wrongfully deprives the bailee of the use or possession of the goods bailed, or does them any injury, the bailee is entitled to use such remedies as the owner might have used in the like case if no bailment had been made; and either the bailor or the bailee may bring a suit against a third person for such deprivation or injury. Current-law framing: concurrent right of action in bailor or bailee against wrong-doers.

examples.title: Suit against wrong-doer
examples.body: Third person wrongfully takes goods from the bailee. Either the bailor or the bailee may sue under Section 180.

hypotheticals.question: A third person injures the goods in the bailee's possession. Who may sue?
hypotheticals.analysis: Either the bailor or the bailee may bring a suit under Section 180. The bailee may use the remedies the owner could have used.
